name: Altstadt Hall in Tirol
kurzbeschreibung: The historic old town of Hall in Tirol enchants visitors as western Austria's largest medieval core with Hasegg Castle, Mint Tower, and winding cobbled alleys.
beschreibung:
Overview

The storied Old Town of Hall in Tirol (Altstadt Hall in Tirol) stands as one of the best-preserved and most architecturally impressive medieval town centers in the entire Alpine region, spanning an area even larger than the historic center of Innsbruck. Shaped by centuries of lucrative salt mining in the neighboring Halltal and the prestigious relocation of the sovereign mint in the 15th century, Hall flourished as a paramount trading and economic hub on the navigable River Inn waterway. Its picturesque ensemble of stately patrician townhouses, late-Gothic facades, romantic bay windows, and cobblestone arcades captivates cultural travelers, architecture enthusiasts, and casual strollers from all over the world.

Route & Requirements

A leisurely walking tour through the pedestrian zone leads from the central Upper Town Square (Oberer Stadtplatz) with its late-Gothic Town Hall and monumental Saint Nicholas Parish Church through narrow winding alleyways such as Schlossergasse and Arbesgasse down to the formidable Hasegg Castle (Burg Hasegg) and its striking twelve-sided Mint Tower. Visitors can explore the historic fortress complex where the world's very first silver Thaler coin was mechanically minted, laying the historical foundation for the modern dollar. Ascending the wooden stairs of the Mint Tower rewards visitors with a sweeping 360-degree panorama across the Inn Valley, Karwendel mountains, and Tux Alps. Flat, sturdy footwear is recommended for the historic cobblestones; the route is well-suited for all generations.

Visit & Arrival

The public old town streets are freely accessible year-round at any hour. The acclaimed Mint Museum inside Hasegg Castle opens from April through October: Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00 (last entry 16:00). Admission for adults is approx. €9.50, children €6.50, with family tickets available. Public transit connections are exceptional: S-Bahn Tirol (lines S4 and S5) as well as regular VVT regional bus lines link Innsbruck directly to Hall in Tirol in just ten to fifteen minutes. Motorists take the Inntal Autobahn A12 (exit Hall Mitte) and park conveniently at the Unterer Stadtplatz underground parking garage.

Tips

Every Friday morning, the traditional Hall farmers' market enlivens the Upper Town Square with fresh regional specialties from across Tyrol. A stroll into the peaceful garden courtyard of the Damenstift convent is highly recommended, as is exploring the boutique craft workshops and art galleries nestled inside historic vaulted cellars offering local crafts and culinary treats. Take time to relax in the sunny café gardens.
preis: Old town tour free; Hasegg Castle Museum with Mint Tower: adults approx. €9.50, children €6.50
oeffnungszeiten: Old town accessible year-round; Hasegg Castle & Mint Tower Apr–Oct Tue–Sun 10:00–17:00 (winter reduced)
